_comment: pykonal_locext configuration. Paths must be absolute.
_traveltime_dir_help: OPTIONAL. If set, this TAKES PRECEDENCE over traveltime_inventory: grids are stored one HDF5 file per station-phase (NET.STA.PHASE.h5) in this directory, plus a small inventory.h5 master of external links that pykonal reads transparently. Recommended when the plugin grows its inventory on demand: writes touch only the station being built (no exclusive lock on the whole archive), rebuilding after a velocity-model change is a file delete, and a crash mid-write can only damage one station. Grids are stamped with a fingerprint of the velocity model that produced them and are rebuilt automatically when that model changes. Set to null to use the single traveltime_inventory file instead. Plugin-only; pyvorotomo is unaffected.
_edt_ot_wt_help: NonLinLoc's LOCMETH EDT_OT_WT (default true). Each arrival implies its own origin time; at the true hypocentre these agree, and at a point that satisfies many differential times only by coincidence they scatter. The EDT pdf is therefore penalised by the weighted variance of those origin-time estimates, floored at log(1e-5). This compacts the location PDF without giving up outlier robustness, because the weights are the EDT pair probabilities themselves, a bad pick satisfies few pairs and contributes almost nothing. Set false for the plain EDT pair sum.
_edt_exponent_help: Exponent applied to the EDT stack. null (default) means the number of arrivals, which is what NonLinLoc uses. This is no longer a cosmetic choice: the EDT_OT_WT penalty is added after the power, so the exponent sets the balance between the two terms. Set a number only if you know why; 1 gives the raw, broadest EDT surface.
_alpha_help: Adds fractional per-arrival uncertainty proportional to its traveltime, e.g. 20 second traveltime * 0.02 = +0.4 sigma. 2% seems to work better than < 0.01, but adding more beyond this may actually hurt.
_default_pick_error_help: Per-phase default pick uncertainty (seconds; MUST be > 0). Event-level box sizing uses the smallest floor in the map.
_pick_error_help: Observation uncertainty in the EDT objective: each pick's variance is sigma^2 + (alpha * traveltime)^2, where sigma is the pick's own time uncertainty if it has one else default_pick_error (seconds, the fixed picking error), and alpha is a fractional model error that grows with traveltime.
_outlier_help: Iterative residual-based arrival rejection. After locating, arrivals whose residual deviates from the median by more than max(outlier_cutoff_s, outlier_mad_factor * MAD) are dropped and the event is relocated, up to 3 passes, never going below outlier_min_arrivals. The MAD term adapts to how noisy the event is; the absolute floor stops a very clean event rejecting picks that are only slightly worse than its excellent others. Rejected arrivals are NOT deleted from the output - they appear with weight 0 and timeUsed false so the analyst sees which were dropped, and the reported RMS is over the used arrivals (making it comparable to NonLinLoc). Set outlier_cutoff_s to 0 to disable. Note EDT already ignores such picks when locating so this mainly fixes reporting and removes competing likelihood modes.
_auto_search_min_help: Absolute floor on the auto half-widths [lat,lon,depth] in km. With the search now seeded at the anchor rather than the box centre, a box that is too small no longer fails gracefully: the search cannot wander into a solution outside it, so an under-resolved sigma produces a confident location at the anchor. auto_search_max_km still overrides these.
_auto_search_depth_dist_help: Depth half-width floor as a fraction of the distance to the NEAREST contributing station. Heuristic: beyond roughly one focal depth the takeoff angle stops changing with depth and the arrival constrains origin time rather than depth, so depth is not resolvable much better than the nearest offset regardless of how small the residuals are. Set 0 to disable.
_auto_search_posterior_help: Samples used in the PROVISIONAL pass to measure the location sigma that sizes the real search box. 0 falls back to the linearised C = s^2 (G^T G)^-1 prediction, which assumes independent residuals and is optimistic (especially wrt depth) wherever the velocity model produces residuals that trend with distance. This is not the reported uncertainty; that is still posterior_nsamples.
_search_delta_auto_help: search_delta_km may be a [lat,lon,depth] list OR the string "auto" (recommended!): auto sizes the box per event as auto_search_k * the predicted 1-sigma location uncertainty per axis, from C=sigma^2(G^T G)^-1 on the traveltime gradients at the initial hypocenter. Tight for well-constrained events, wider for gappy ones; each event logs sigma, half-widths and conditioning. auto_search_max_km caps each axis [lat,lon,depth]; auto_search_cond_max flags weak/degenerate-depth geometry above that cond.
_search_delta_help: Half-widths of the search box in km, in the order [north-south, east-west, depth], centred on search_anchor. NOTE this order differs from the internal grid axis order, which is [depth, north-south, east-west] for spherical grids. Sizing rule: each half-width should be at least 4x the uncertainty you expect on that axis. Below that the posterior is truncated at the box edge and the reported uncertainty becomes a lower bound rather than a measurement.
_posterior_help: Monte-Carlo samples used AFTER the location to characterize its uncertainty: the EDT likelihood is sampled around the solution to build the confidence ellipsoid and the lat/lon/depth uncertainties written to the origin and shown in scolv. Sampling is ADAPTIVE and contracts geometrically around the solution (floored at 4 sigma) over up to 6 passes - because a single uniform draw over a wide search box lands almost no samples near the peak. The solution log reports 'ess=' (effective sample size); values below ~50 mean the uncertainty is poorly resolved and the run warns. If you see that, raise this value or narrow search_delta_km. 2048 is a reasonable default; raised for smoother ellipsoids. Set 0 to skip uncertainty estimation entirely. EDT only; ignored for method 'l1'.
_search_anchor_help: Where to CENTER the search box (center +/- search_delta_km). 'origin' (DEFAULT, recommended) = the input origin. 'stations' = station centroid + default_depth; this makes the location a pure function of the picks (successive scolv relocations become idempotent, since scolv feeds each result back as the next initial origin), BUT it only works if search_delta_km is small enough that the sampling stays dense - with a wide box the search must find the event blind from the network centroid and does much worse. 'grid_center' = cfg grid_center. If you using 'stations', narrow search_delta_km first!
_posterior_seed_help: Fixed random seed for posterior sampling, or null (DEFAULT) for independent draws each relocation. null is recommended: with adaptive sampling the uncertainties are now stable run-to-run, and leaving it unseeded means genuine sampling problems stay visible rather than being frozen behind a fixed seed. Set an integer only if you need bit-identical repeatability.
_confidence_level_help: Confidence level in PERCENT for the reported uncertainties. 68 (default) matches NonLinLoc. The confidence ELLIPSOID is the three-dimensional region at this level (1.878 sigma at 68%), horizontalUncertainty is the two-dimensional horizontal region (1.515 sigma), and the per-axis latitude/longitude/depth uncertainties are one-dimensional marginals (1.000 sigma). Earlier versions emitted bare 1-sigma semi-axes labelled as a confidence ellipsoid, which made pykonal ellipsoids look about half the linear size of NonLinLoc's for the same posterior. Set 95 to report 95% regions instead.
_velocity_models_help: pykonal ScalarField3D HDF5 files per phase. If set, any station/phase in the picks that has no stored traveltime grid is computed ONCE (FMM solve) and persisted before locating; later runs and concurrent processes reuse it. Omit to disable on-the-fly computation (unknown stations are then dropped with a warning).
_solve_n_closest_help: If > 0, solve the hypocenter using only the N geographically closest arrivals (ranked by epicentral distance from the initial origin), while STILL reporting residuals, weights and timeUsed for every arrival and keeping them in the solution. Distant arrivals in a 1D model carry Pn/model error that can drag the solution; restricting the solve to nearby stations that sample the represented crust can sharpen the hypocenter without discarding the far arrivals from the output. Arrivals lacking station coordinates cannot be ranked and are always report-only. Outlier rejection still uses all residuals to decide what is bad but relocates on the closest set. 0 = use all arrivals to solve (default).
_depth_help: OPTIONAL physical bounds (km) on the depth search. depth_min = shallowest allowed (negative permits solutions above the datum, e.g. -1.0 allows 1 km above sea level); depth_max = deepest allowed. The symmetric search box (anchor depth +/- search_delta_km[2]) is recentered and its depth half-width shrunk to stay within [depth_min, depth_max]. Remove BOTH keys to disable clamping. You may set just one, e.g. only depth_max to cap depth while leaving the top open for station elevation.
_ensure_nproc_help: parallel FMM solves when several grids are missing at once; null = min(n_missing, cpu_count), 1 = serial
_stations_help: optional CSV 'NET,STA,lat,lon,elev_m'. Enables azimuthal gap, arrival distances/azimuths, and --max-dist filtering.
_log_arrival_detail_help: Log per-arrival distance, predicted traveltime, implied apparent velocity and residual. Use to diagnose large residuals: if apparent velocities exceed your velocity model, the traveltime grids were built from a model that is too fast. Note EDT locates on differential times, so a systematic traveltime error cancels in the hypocenter and is absorbed by the origin time - the location can match another locator while absolute residuals remain large.
